//: Point the Bit extension at the brew-installed compiler. An ABSOLUTE path, not `bit` on PATH: VS Code launched from the Dock does not inherit the shell PATH. Apple Silicon prefix; on an Intel Mac this is /usr/local/bin/bit.
//2: This was ${userHome}/.local/bin/bit, the bare binary editors/install-local.sh drops in. Two reasons brew's copy is the better server: it ships the whole tree (bin + stdlib + lib), so the server resolves stdlib from its own install location instead of whatever it can find near the file being edited; and it is the exact build users get, so editor diagnostics match what a `brew install` compiles.
//3: The tradeoff, deliberately accepted: the server is the RELEASED compiler, so a language feature still in the working tree reads as an error in the editor until the next release lands. When that bites, point this back at ${userHome}/.local/bin/bit for the duration.
